endorsements.quote: Patients must be explicitly informed if their surgical video logs, clinical outcomes, or biological data will be utilized to train proprietary AI models or optimize robotic software [ 1 , 5 ].

Clinicians must restore to patients the definitive ability to decide how their most intimate clinical data is utilized, ensuring they are treated as an end in themselves and never as a mere commodity to be sold off [ 5 ].

unlisted_practices: Expand informed consent forms to address the patient's digital footprint, including a Digital Sovereignty Addendum.
Consent protocols should state where the patient's digital data will be stored, who controls the underlying models, and whether the data will be monetized or transferred to private third parties.
Use AI strictly as an assistant that reduces administrative friction rather than letting automated systems dictate patient pathways or resource allocation without strict human oversight.

screen.reason: This is an editorial providing ethical recommendations and framework proposals (including informed consent updates) for surgical AI governance.
